ref.note: Grant to two other governments: COCOF and the VGC decide how they spend it. Most of it is fixed by the Special Act of 12 January 1989 on the Brussels institutions: drawing rights (art. 83quater) and special dotations for former provincial education and other former provincial tasks (art. 83ter), see the VGC plan p. 38 (PDF p. 44): 'Het ingeschreven bedrag wordt bepaald bij artikel 83quater van de bijzondere wet van 12 januari 1989'. The education phrase rests on the dotations named in the line itself ('... pour le financement de l'enseignement', former provincial schools). The VGC also invests in school buildings (ACT116: 'De VGC zet in op het behoud en de uitbreiding van de onderwijscapaciteit en investeert in de bouw en de verbouwing van scholen'). COCOF's spending (e.g. disability services via its Service PHARE) could not be checked in its own budget: parlementfrancophone.brussels and ccf.brussels are blocked, and the PHARE page (Service PHARE (personnes en situation de handicap) – page d'accueil (https://phare.irisnet.be/)) is a closure notice listing competences, not spending, so no COCOF-specific service phrase is given. NL uses 'COCOF' as in the line label (official Dutch name: Franse Gemeenschapscommissie, FGC). COCOF's grant is about 78% of this line, VGC about 22%. corrected: flag 2: first phrase now says plainly that the money is passed on to COCOF and the VGC; COCOF disability phrase dropped (rested only on the PHARE closure page, not solid; COCOF budget blocked) and replaced by a schools phrase grounded in the line's own allocations (annex 5a pp. 320-321, education dotations to both commissions); VGC childcare phrase kept (ACT241 confirmed at PDF p. 25); source changed to the annex 5a concordance
